items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: The interviewee (Jerry Blumberg) does not mention Simon. The mention of 'Metronome editor, Simon' comes from the Interviewer, and the Interviewee only responds to the anecdote about Bunk playing with one hand, showing no personal connection to Simon.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah, I remember sometimes... Well, he was always leafing through his music. He had a big stack of lead sheets up there of all these different tunes. And he'd be sitting there sometimes playing, holding the horn up with one hand. And it didn't make any difference to him whether it was the right hand or the left hand. He'd just... Sometimes he'd play through a couple choruses with his left hand, holding the horn and fingering it with the left hand, which isn't an exceptionally difficult thing. But it didn't…

I can remember one night. That's about the second or third week the band first opened there. And the Metronome editor, Simon, or whoever his name was, went to Leonard Feather. And there's two or three other people from Metronome, I think, were there. Not Feather, but some other people. And Bunk sort of put on an act for him. He'd play with one hand. I guess his right hand. He'd hold the horn with the right hand and the finger. And he'd be buttoning his coat.
He was always doing things like that. So he could play with one hand.
